a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every system N of type S1 X Y there exists a system N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has at least one index, and for every ordered pair of its indices m, n there is a directed chain of one or more dependency edges from m to n. This includes m = n, for which a chain of length zero does not count. An edge from i to j means that there exist two full state assignments of N′ and an input x in X such that the assignments agree at every index other than i, but updating j with that same input x gives different values on the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) The number of indices of N′ is exactly the number of indices of N plus one; no inclusion of the old indices in the new ones is required. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs in Y when each starts from its own initial assignment, processes the list from left to right, and applies its own output function to its final assignment. Equality of internal states is not required. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or connectivity hypothesis on N."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every system N of type S1 X Y there exists a system N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has at least one index, and for every ordered pair of its indices m, n there is a directed chain of one or more dependency edges from m to n. This includes m = n, for which a chain of length zero does not count. An edge from i to j means that there exist two full state assignments of N′ and an input x in X such that the assignments agree at every index other than i, but updating j with that same input x gives different values on the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) The number of indices of N′ is exactly the number of indices of N plus one; no inclusion of the old indices in the new ones is required. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs in Y when each starts from its own initial assignment, processes the list from left to right, and applies its own output function to its final assignment. Equality of internal states is not required. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or connectivity hypothesis on N.

divergences.description: The description calls agreement on every finite history a strict strengthening of P2. P2 requires equality of the entire input-output function and specifies no time cutoff. If that function maps finite histories to outputs, its equality already requires agreement on every such history. Appendix A likewise preserves F(x) for every x without specifying whether x is a history. The Lean statement makes the temporal model explicit, but the passages do not support the claimed strict comparison on this point.

judgement.summary: The Lean proposition matches the author's description: for nonempty X, one twin satisfies the structural loop condition, has exactly one more unit, and matches the original on all finite histories. The contrast concerning ϕ is accurate for p. 52 and Appendix A; P2 itself makes no ϕ claim.
